summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, and GERD was admitted for chills and markedly elevated liver enzymes. He was found to have cholangitis due to Citrobacter freundii bacteremia, confirmed by blood cultures. He was started on meropenem, and an ERCP revealed bile duct strictures that were stented. His immunosuppressant sirolimus was reduced from 3 mg to 2 mg daily during the infection. Renal function, which was initially impaired with creatinine at 3.0, improved to 1.5 with oral hydration. Liver enzymes normalized significantly by discharge. A PICC line was placed for outpatient IV ertapenem to complete a 14-day course. He was discharged home in stable condition with plans for follow-up and a repeat ERCP in six months.
